conclusion.summary: All six obligations were independently assessed. The core selector, dotfile, broken-link and case analyses are mostly supported, but the unconditional unreadable-root-raises conclusion and proposed own-root chmod(0) expectation are incorrect. Iterator-error, file-type and stable-tree qualifications constrain the completeness recommendation.

findings.title: Unreadable root is not an unconditional exception boundary
findings.semantic_correction: Distinguish EACCES/EPERM in initial root stat/is_dir (propagated) from a root's scandir opening/listing failure (suppressed in the wildcard path and opening suppressed in walk). Own-root chmod(0) can produce an empty result rather than raise.
findings.actual_check: K05: under euid 1000, mode-000 root stat succeeded and scandir raised PermissionError errno 13; mode-000 ancestor made root stat raise PermissionError errno 13. This is an OS primitive witness on Python 3.14.4, not a CPython 3.12.3 rglob run.
findings.preservation: Inherited from intermediate-1 candidate, accepted by intermediate-2, and carried unchanged through intermediates 3/4 and final.

findings.title: Walk scan-iterator errors are not covered by the opening-error suppression
findings.semantic_correction: Limit suppression claims to the actual protected calls. walk context/iterator errors outside its try can propagate through rglob; the implementation governs over the broader documentation sentence.
findings.actual_check: K03 AST and direct line inspection establish exception scopes. No fault injection or real iterator-error witness executed.

findings.title: Tree stability is required by the exact-completeness and never-follow claims
findings.semantic_correction: Qualify conclusions for a stable tree. Concurrent membership changes are unspecified, and a directory replaced by a symlink after classification can still be traversed.
findings.actual_check: Direct released-source/documentation inspection; no race witness executed.

claim_groups.assessment: rglob parses the relative pattern, prepends **, builds recursive and wildcard successor selectors, and checks the starting root with is_dir. A non-directory or ignored missing/broken root yields no results. More exactly, recursion yields the root and each dirnames child discovered by walk, including children whose later scan may fail.

Wildcard matching closes each scandir snapshot before yielding; it suppresses OSError from opening and consuming that snapshot. Dironly successors use entry.is_dir() and skip its OSError. The final *.csv component is not dironly and tests only names. Path._scandir delegates to os.scandir; fnmatch.translate is compiled with case flags. The cited many-open-files test is a source test definition, not an executed witness.

For a stable tree, descendant symlink directories are classified as filenames by walk(follow_symlinks=False), so recursive ** does not visit their alias paths. This does not prevent matching the symlink name itself or traversing a symlink supplied as the starting root; is_dir/stat follows that root. A link target also reachable by a real directory path inside the root can still be inventoried there. The unconditional word never needs the stability qualification described in C11.

Explicit wildcard directory positions call DirEntry.is_dir() with follow_symlinks=True, then scan the matched path. glob('*/x.csv') can reach an immediate linked directory; rglob('*/fileB') source tests likewise enumerate linked aliases when symlinks are available. This is a finite explicit-component behavior, not recursive following by **.

fnmatch translation and the wildcard selector have no leading-period exclusion. *.csv matches .hidden.csv at the root and every scanned depth, including under real hidden directories. fnmatch explicitly says an initial period is not special. The final's statement about no dotfile-specific glob test is supported by a bounded search of the single frozen pathscan file, not a claim about all CPython tests.

A dangling b.csv is yielded by a final non-dironly name match, but cannot be followed through a required directory component. The loop and 50/50-link test definitions support the distinction. The wording is_dir returns False only on ignored errnos is literally incomplete: normal non-directory stat results and ValueError also return False. In the OSError branch, only ignored errno/winerror values return False; other OSError propagates. The actual _IGNORED_ERRNOS definition is line 45, not 48.

case_sensitive=None uses the path flavour normcase probe. POSIX default is case-sensitive and Windows default insensitive; True/False override the name matcher, using re.IGNORECASE for False. Z.CSV is included by *.csv under the insensitive choice. The keyword was added in 3.12. Shared glob test definitions are relevant to rglob's same selector. This is matching policy, not an automatic probe of each filesystem directory's case or normalization rules.

Unreadable root does not generally imply a propagated error. An EACCES/EPERM from the initial root is_dir/stat propagates, but a root that can be statted and cannot be listed gets its wildcard and walk-opening scandir failures suppressed and can yield an empty inventory. Own-root chmod(0) ordinarily creates that latter situation under an unprivileged POSIX user. A denied ancestor search can create the former. Root versus subdirectory is therefore the wrong sole boundary; operation and exception location govern. The reviewer OS-only witness confirmed stat succeeds/scandir fails for mode-000 root, and stat fails for a root behind a mode-000 ancestor. It did not execute release-specific pathlib.

Denied subdirectory scan opening normally silently omits its descendants; a denied entry.is_dir in walk classifies it as a filename. However, walk's try covers only _scandir() construction at 1129. Errors during context entry/iteration/exit at 1135-1138 are outside it and can propagate through rglob; unlike wildcard snapshot iteration, walk iteration is not protected. The glob documentation's broad subsequent-scanning suppression sentence is not fully implemented by this release-specific walk path. Y does not disclose that boundary. No injected or real I/O-iteration failure was run.

rglob('*.csv') is a name inventory of entries of any kind, not intrinsically a regular-file inventory. A real directory called data.csv, a directory symlink called alias.csv, or another matching non-file can be yielded; the terminal wildcard does no type check. Y correctly notices broken-link inclusion but does not give a file-type policy for its sound inventory primitive recommendation. Whether a later is_file filter is wanted is an unresolved product definition, not a candidate edit made here.

The source explicitly assumes a tree is not modified during walk. A real directory can be replaced by a symlink after classification and still be descended with follow_symlinks=False; scandir also leaves membership unspecified during concurrent additions/removals. Listing every reachable directory is therefore necessary but not sufficient for the final's exact-completeness promise. Require a stable tree or qualify the inventory as an observation during traversal. No mutation witness was run.

All five proposed check families are clearly marked not executed. Dotfiles at two depths, a dangling .csv, and default/explicit case variants have sound predictions. The linked-directory fixture should put its target outside the root or assert alias paths so a real in-tree target is not mistaken for traversal through a link. The permission family has a wrong own-root chmod(0)->raise expectation; separate denied stat from denied listing and verify permissions are effective under the test identity. The candidate ran none of these as far as the mapped text reports; independent execution history is unassessed.

All ten supplied hashes match the current mapped bytes, including every candidate artifact. All five primary files independently re-fetched from public v3.12.3 URLs match those same hashes and byte counts. This verifies source identity at review time and source linkage, not the asserted original fetch time or which original stage executed sha256sum. Source manifest and brief also have review-computed full hashes. Additional sources are legitimately allowed by brief line 14 and close dependencies at the same release.

Principal entry, selector, scanning, case, test, walk and additional-source ranges contain the cited support. _IGNORED_ERRNOS line 48 is wrong (definition line 45); is_dir 870-876 cuts off its raise/False/ValueError handling at 877-884. The trailing rglob case keyword range 1081-1097 identifies signatures, while version addition is actually established by docs 945-946 and 1358-1359. The '*.csv' suffix's regex translation is fully returned at fnmatch line 185. These citation defects do not cause the central root-error inference; even the complete ranges refute it.

Every intermediate and the final preserve all six obligation topics. Navigation marks dotfile and DirEntry-default claims as candidates; focused read preserves those open dependencies; expansion resolves both using mapped same-release fnmatch/os sources; final carries the resolution and proposed-only checks. No predecessor requirement is silently dropped. The bad root-raises inference is promoted from a candidate in intermediate-1 to accepted in intermediate-2 and propagated unchanged through expansion and finalization; the claimed re-verification did not correct it. The final and intermediate-4 share scope but are different bytes/lengths; equivalent scope is supported, byte identity is not asserted here. Prior intermediate findings were visible and used for this preservation assessment.

The added same-release sources provide supported useful closure for dotfile matching and explicit-component symlink following. The latter is a useful contrast beyond plain *.csv recursion, directly relevant to obligation 3. DT_UNKNOWN can require extra metadata system calls; however, the additional call may fail (DirEntry docs explicitly allow OSError), so without changing match outcomes is only a successful-call/stable-tree simplification, not a universal assurance. No extra scientific yield, novelty, cost, winner or native-success score is inferred.

Version pinning, mutable-main limits, unexercised Windows error branches, and macOS normalization limits are disclosed appropriately; rglob doc has no separate error paragraph but links its behavior to glob. Code-based inference is legitimate and not itself an unresolved defect. More consequential uncertainty about stat versus listing, walk iterator exceptions, file-type semantics and tree stability is missing. Windows execution, unusual filesystems and normalization behavior remain untested by this review; no current-release generalization is made.

Original no-execution/no-installer/no-edit/no-delegation/no-sibling-access statements, per-stage re-verification/fetch timestamps, delivery paths, native Goal activation/terminal receipts and deadlines are recorded candidate assertions only. No lifecycle, parent-state, identity-map, case-card, other-review or receipt files were opened. Frozen text can show no claimed runtime test and method disclosures, but cannot prove execution history. The complete scientific claims in C01-C17 were independently assessed; this limitation is not a reduction of scientific scope.
